info.title: Kaal Jyoti API
info.description: Vedic astrology calculations — kundli, panchang, dashas, divisional charts and more — each priced in credits, every API on every plan. Planetary positions from NASA JPL’s DE440 ephemeris.

ValidationError.description: The request was not valid (`validation_error`); `field` names the offender.

QuotaExceeded.description: This month's credits, and any credit packs, cannot cover the request (`quota_exceeded`). A publishable key also gets it at its own daily credit cap, and does not draw on packs unless its owner allows it.

Forbidden.description: The key may not call this: a PDF on the Free plan or a publishable key on a server-only route (`plan_required`), or a publishable key from an origin that is not allowed (`forbidden_origin`).

NotComputable.description: Valid, but not computable for this moment and place (`not_computable`) — a circumpolar sunrise, for instance.

ServiceDisabled.description: The API is switched off for maintenance (`service_disabled`).

LabelledId.description: An id the gateway has named. The engine answers in stable snake_case ids (`sun`, `cancer`, `purva_phalguni`); every field that holds one is published as this object instead of as a bare string, so a client can show `name` and still switch on `id`. The panchang limbs, vara, masa and paksha use the same kind of id (`pratipada`, `somavara`, `shukla`). Ask for several languages (`options.language`) and `names` carries one entry per language.

id.description: The stable id, e.g. `sun` — switch on this.

name.description: The name in the first requested language.

names.description: One name per requested language; present when more than one was asked for.

name.description: IANA zone, or null when a bare offset was given.

source.description: `derived` means the gateway looked the zone up from the coordinates.

cached.description: The answer came from the cache.

id.description: The slug that was used, e.g. `lahiri`.

value.description: Degrees, when the op reports one.

engine.description: Engine version the answer was computed with.

language_fallback.description: Languages that were asked for but have no labels.

credits.description: Credits this request cost — also in the `X-KJ-Credits` header. `GET /v1/reference/credits` lists what every route costs.

get.description: What this instance loaded: the engine and ephemeris versions, the number of ops, the dates it answers for (`supported_range`, from its ephemeris data) and how long it has been up. No key needed, and it keeps answering while the service is disabled.

200.description: The answer.

supported_range.description: The dates the API answers for, from its ephemeris data: calendar dates at the place, whole months; `first_year`/`last_year` bound the whole-year fields (a Varshphal `year`). A date outside is a 400.

get.description:
The API's own vocabulary: every id an answer can contain and the name to show for it. One of `ayanamsas`, `planets`, `signs`, `nakshatras`, `tithis`, `yogas`, `karanas`, `vargas`, `dasha-systems`, `house-systems`, `chalit-systems`, `transit-events`, `languages`, `credits`. Add `?language=hi` (or `?language=hi,en`) for translated names. 

`credits` lists what every route costs, in credits, right now. Free: these cost no credits and may be cached for a day (`credits` for a minute).

schema.description: Comma-separated label languages, `en` and `hi`, e.g. `hi,en`: the first is the one `name` carries. Default `en`.

parameters.description: Comma-separated label languages, `en` and `hi`, e.g. `hi,en`: the first is the one `name` carries. Default `en`.
parameters.name: language

200.description: The answer.

items.description: An `{id, name}` row — or `{index, name}` for the tables the engine numbers (tithis, yogas, karanas), plus whatever else that list publishes. `credits` is `{route, credits, per?}`: the route path, its price, and `pair` or `part` when that price is per unit.

get.description:
The IANA zone covering a coordinate and the UTC offset it was on at `datetime` (default: now) — historical offsets included, so 1944 in India answers `+06:30`. 

Free: this costs no credits, and is rate limited like the reference tables.

schema.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, north positive, from -89.9 to 89.9, e.g. `28.6139`.

parameters.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, north positive, from -89.9 to 89.9, e.g. `28.6139`.
parameters.name: lat

schema.description: Longitude in decimal degrees, east positive, from -180 to 180, e.g. `77.209`.

parameters.description: Longitude in decimal degrees, east positive, from -180 to 180, e.g. `77.209`.
parameters.name: lon

schema.description: The local clock time at the point to read the offset at, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, e.g. `1944-03-15T10:00:00` (Delhi then: `+06:30`). Default: now.

get.description:
A small built-in place search: towns and cities of 1,000 people or more, not villages. For a full search use a geocoder (Google Places or any other) and send only `latitude` and `longitude` in the `birth` — the API derives the time zone in force at that moment.

Places whose name begins with `q`, best match first and then the most populous, searched in Latin or Devanagari script, with former names for the larger ones ("Bombay" finds Mumbai). **Heavy route** (†): a separate limit of 10 requests a minute, on every plan.

Costs 20 credits.

**The example answer is shortened:** long lists (`data.nirayan.days`, `data.nirayan.events`) show only their first 3 items. A real answer has them all.
